headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: dbt-core can feed warehouse data into Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing context, creating default exfiltration and trust-chain hazards.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core has no documented shared channel to Perplexity, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, Perplexity can ingest uploaded documents and browsing context, and dbt-core works with warehouse data that could be copied into prompts or files. The pathway is indirect and requires manual bridging, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs are manually pasted or uploaded into Perplexity
IF Perplexity is asked to interpret dbt-generated text as instructions
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste policy that strips instructions from dbt outputs
Label dbt artifacts as data-only before uploading
Review Perplexity prompts for instruction-like text before submission

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, and Perplexity is vendor-hosted with uploaded documents and browsing context. Even without a shared filesystem, moving warehouse extracts or dbt artifacts into Perplexity can expose sensitive data to a third-party inference backend in default workflows. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible and not blocked by default.
conditions: IF warehouse data or dbt artifacts are uploaded into Perplexity
IF the uploaded material contains sensitive warehouse records
mitigations: Restrict Perplexity use to non-sensitive summaries
Confirm uploads are excluded from sensitive datasets

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core does not request filesystem write, git modification, or broad OAuth scopes, while Perplexity cannot write the host filesystem or modify git state. The main overlap is read/analysis of user-provided content, so direct mutable-resource conflict is unlikely. Uncertainty is low because the profiles explicitly block the dangerous write surfaces.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable workspace
IF dbt-core is wrapped in tooling that adds filesystem or git write permissions
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only inputs
Separate workspaces for dbt and Perplexity
Audit any wrapper that adds write permissions

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity’s answer-engine workflow can treat uploaded content and browsing context as authoritative, while dbt-core produces analytics artifacts that may be reused as source material. If Perplexity renders or acts on dbt outputs without verification, errors can cascade into reports or decisions. The interaction is plausible in default usage, though not directly documented for this pair.
conditions: IF dbt-generated metrics or SQL explanations are pasted into Perplexity
IF Perplexity outputs are reused without independent validation
mitigations: Require a second-source check for any dbt-derived claim
Ask Perplexity to cite primary warehouse queries
Compare outputs against dbt run artifacts
Mark Perplexity summaries as untrusted until reviewed

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches warehouse data, and Perplexity is a closed-source vendor-hosted service with uploaded documents and browsing context. If regulated or residency-bound data is moved from dbt workflows into Perplexity, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is uploaded to Perplexity
IF the data subject to residency or retention rules is included in prompts or files
mitigations: Check vendor retention settings before upload
Route compliance-sensitive questions to an approved internal tool
